meta.purpose: Distinguish active, production-ready features from deprecated, removed, dev-only, or partial features

featureStatusInventory.details: Routes /phone-login and /verify-otp are hardcoded to redirect to /login. PhoneLogin.tsx is a stub returning <Navigate to="/login" replace />. Phone verification is now consolidated into VerifyPhone.tsx.
Route /map redirects to /explore. Map browsing is embedded directly inside ExplorePage.tsx via the Map toggle switch rather than living on its own route.
Guarded by import.meta.env.DEV. The entire /dev/seed route and SeedData.tsx bundle are tree-shaken and excluded from production builds.

Modals exist in src/components/ for DigiLocker and Aadhaar OTP verification. However, government DigiLocker API credentials are not integrated; actual identity verification in production operates via document file upload (OwnerVerificationGate.tsx) with human admin review in AdminVerifications.tsx.
CreateTeamModal component is implemented with team name, budget, and member selection inputs, but is not currently linked to any primary navigation item or dashboard CTA in the active application.

usePushNotifications hook initializes Firebase Messaging and requests browser notification permissions, storing fcmToken in the user's Firestore document. However, since NestMate has no Node backend or deployed Cloud Functions, background push dispatch on incoming chat messages or inquiries is not active.

Firestore security rules provide complete permission rules for agreements and agreementOTPs collections, and jspdf is included in package.json dependencies, but the end-to-end multi-party signing UI is partially implemented.

mukvr46@gmail.com, admin@nestmate.in, and admin@nestmate-test.com are hardcoded as authorized admin emails in firestore.rules and useAdmin.ts as a bootstrap mechanism before admins/{email} documents are provisioned.
Enforced on client-side before creating a connection document. Firestore security rules enforce connection validation but quota count enforcement relies on client application logic.
Firestore rules explicitly permit anonymous / guest clients to increment the 'views' field on a listing without authentication, ensuring view statistics function for public browsing.
